Subject: Privatenet evidence: offline update delivery / operator access question

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the quick engagement so far. As part of our compliance review we need a focused response on two narrow but high-risk items for our on-prem (air-gapped) deployment:

1) How does Redwood deliver signed updates to an air-gapped cluster? We need chain-of-custody and verification details for the on-site image (signed binaries, manifest, how to validate SHA256 and signing certs).

2) Operator access model for emergency support: we need to understand time-limited access tokens, operator credential scoping, and whether we can require key escrow / identity proofs prior to any elevated session. Please include any runbooks or evidence artifacts.

We attached a short RFI with the fields we need filled; happy to take this over a short call as well.

Attachment: Heptagon_RFI_attachments_list.pdf (1 page)

Appreciate the detailed response by Friday US close.

Regards,
Anita Rao
Head of IT Security
Heptagon Medical

Subject: Re: Privatenet evidence: offline update delivery / operator access question

Anita — thank you, and absolutely. High-level answers first, attached is an evidence pack and a short operational runbook. If anything needs deeper cryptographic proof (cert chain, signing key material handling) we can redact private keys and provide signed manifests plus notarized audit statements.

Summary (short):
- Offline updates: We publish signed install images and a human-readable manifest. On-prem teams receive a signed artifact bundle (.tar.gpg) delivered via controllable channels (SFTP, signed USB, or sealed courier). Each bundle contains: signed-install-image.sha256, manifest.json.asc (deterministic ordering), and a PKI-signed certificate chain you can use to validate. Verification steps are in the attached text artifact (redwood-offline-update-manifest.txt).
- Chain-of-custody: Every bundle has a manifest and a changelist with timestamp, CI run id, and the operator who packaged it. For physical transfers we provide a custody form and SHA256 envelope seals; for SFTP transfers we use ephemeral one-time URLs with two-person release.
- Operator access: We support time‑boxed support sessions via short-lived, per-deployment provisioning tokens (EPHEMERAL tokens minted by customer KMS or Redwood CA). Access requires multi-factor operator identity (cert + OTP) and explicit customer-initiated approval (console action or signed approval email). Full session recording and optional keystroke capture for auditors is available.

Attachments sent: redwood-offline-update-manifest.txt (verification steps), signed-install-image.sha256 (artifact checksum), operator_runbook_v1.2.pdf (runbook + access policy), Heptagon_RFI_attachments_list.pdf (returned with fields filled).

I'll coordinate with Ben and Irene to add the custody form and a sample notarized statement. Will follow up with the signed custody PDF by tomorrow.

Next step: propose a brief 30-min walkthrough on Friday 11:00 AM ET to step through the verification flow and confirm acceptance criteria. Does that work for your team?

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Manager, Solutions Engineering — Redwood Inference

Dr. Rao — attaching the requested artifacts and a concise playbook to validate offline updates and operator sessions. Key points below and attachments referenced: 

1) Signed offline bundles (what you receive)
- Bundle contents (attached): signed-install-<version>.tar.gpg, signed-install-image.sha256, redwood-offline-update-manifest.txt, packaging_changelog.txt.asc
- How to verify: run verify.sh (included) which performs: check SHA256 -> validate GPG signature -> verify certificate chain against our CA root -> cross-check CI build id and release tag. Steps are enumerated in redwood-offline-update-manifest.txt (see attachment).

2) Chain-of-custody and physical transfer
- For USB / courier deliveries we provide a custody_form_HEP_signed.pdf (sample attached) which contains courier seal IDs and timestamps. The manifest includes a custody field with signer DN and packaging operator id.

3) Operator access and emergency support model
- Short-lived provisioning tokens: Expire after 30 minutes (configurable), minted either by your KMS (recommended) or Redwood CA. Tokens are bound to a deployment ID and IP-range.
- Session gating: Customer-approved console action or signed email is required to enable privileged session. All sessions are recorded and hashes of the recordings are added to the packaging audit record.
- We support offline justification workflows (customer signs an approval PDF and exchanges it via SFTP) if your environment disallows interactive approvals.

4) Artifacts and evidence attached
- Heptagon_RFI_attachments_list.pdf (your original; we filled the RFI fields)
- redwood-offline-update-manifest.txt (verification checklist + manifest schema)
- signed-install-image.sha256 (artifact checksum)
- custody_form_HEP_signed.pdf (sample, redacted)
- operator_runbook_v1.2.pdf (runbook: access flows, revocation, post-session audit)

5) Optional: HSM escrow / notarized signing
- If you require an additional layer, we can arrange HSM-backed signing and a notarized attestation (we work with a hardware partner) and provide a contract addendum.

Next steps:
- Please confirm whether you prefer physical courier or secure SFTP for the initial bundle delivery.
- Let's hold a 30-min walkthrough on Monday 14 May at 11:00 AM ET (I proposed Friday earlier but timing worked better for your ops folks). I sent a calendar invite to Dr. Rao and her security team; please accept or propose another slot.

If you'd like, we can red-team the verification steps during the walkthrough (we bring a small test artifact and do a live validate).

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out quickly.

Best regards,
Tessa Morgan
